pitchEn: Auto Sound Diagnostics listens to your car through the microphone (engine, running gear, brakes, cabin), analyses acoustic features on-device and suggests possible causes with general advice. It is a rough guide only, NOT an exact diagnosis, and it never replaces a qualified mechanic.
newFeaturesEn: 1.0021: Native microphone recording (Android AudioRecord) — works on every EMUI/HarmonyOS device, even where the in-app browser refused the microphone; the recording is a temporary file that is deleted right after the on-device analysis. Plus: record the car sound (engine, running gear, brakes, cabin), choose where/when it occurs, get possible causes with urgency and advice, in 15 languages.

dataHandling.notes: The microphone is used only while you tap 'Record & analyze'; the audio is recorded natively (Android AudioRecord) as a temporary WAV file in the app's private cache, analysed on-device and the file is deleted right after the analysis; it is NEVER uploaded. Network is used only to translate the result text into your chosen language via MyMemory (free, keyless) — skipped for Bulgarian and when offline — plus the common Pupikes layer (optional anonymous help report and self-promotion catalogue). No account, no personal data. Only your language and app preferences are stored on-device.

reviewerRemarksEn: No login or account. On first launch: a short Pupikes intro, then choose a language, then a MANDATORY disclaimer screen (informational only, not an exact diagnosis, not a replacement for a mechanic; do not use while driving) with an 'I understand' checkbox that must be ticked to continue. Then pick where/when the sound occurs and tap 'Record & analyze' — the app listens for a few seconds and shows possible causes with advice. The microphone permission (RECORD_AUDIO) is the only permission and is used solely for this on-device analysis; the recording is a temporary file deleted right after the analysis; nothing is transmitted. Recording is native (Android AudioRecord), so it works on EMUI/HarmonyOS devices where the WebView refused getUserMedia.
